questions.q: Two identical bodies $A$ and $B$ of equal masses have initial velocities $\vec{v_1} = 4\hat{i}$ m/s and $\vec{v_2} = 4\hat{j}$ m/s respectively. The body $A$ has acceleration $\vec{a_1} = 6\hat{i} + 6\hat{j}$ m/s$^2$ while the acceleration of the other body $B$ is zero. The centre of mass of the two bodies moves in __________ path.
questions.solution:
Velocity of the centre of mass is given by:

$\vec{v}_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1\vec{v}_1 + m_2\vec{v}_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

Since $m_1 = m_2 = m$, we get:

$\vec{v}_{cm} = \dfrac{m(4\hat{i}) + m(4\hat{j})}{2m} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$ m/s

Acceleration of the centre of mass is given by:

$\vec{a}_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1\vec{a}_1 + m_2\vec{a}_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

$\vec{a}_{cm} = \dfrac{m(6\hat{i} + 6\hat{j}) + 0}{2m} = 3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ m/s$^2$

Here, $\vec{v}_{cm} = 2(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$ and $\vec{a}_{cm} = 3(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$.

Since the initial velocity and acceleration of the centre of mass are parallel to each other, the centre of mass moves in a straight line path.

Answer: straight line

questions.q: The position of center of mass of three masses $2$ kg, $3$ kg and $15$ kg placed with respect to mid point ($p$) of normal bisector, as shown in the figure is _______.
questions.solution:
Let the midpoint $p$ of the normal bisector be the origin $(0,0)$.

The triangle is isosceles with two sides of $10\text{ m}$ and an included angle of $120^\circ$. The altitude from the $15\text{ kg}$ mass bisects the angle into two $60^\circ$ angles.

The length of the altitude is $10 \cos(60^\circ) = 5\text{ m}$.

Since $p$ is the midpoint of this altitude, the $15\text{ kg}$ mass is at a distance of $2.5\text{ m}$ above $p$, and the base is $2.5\text{ m}$ below $p$.

The distance of the $2\text{ kg} and 3\text{ kg}$ masses from the altitude is $10 \sin(60^\circ) = 5\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$.

The coordinates of the masses with respect to $p$ are:
$m_1 = 15\text{ kg}$ at $(0, 2.5)$
$m_2 = 2\text{ kg}$ at $(-5\sqrt{3}, -2.5)$
$m_3 = 3\text{ kg}$ at $(5\sqrt{3}, -2.5)$

The x-coordinate of the center of mass is:
$x_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1 x_1 + m_2 x_2 + m_3 x_3}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3} = \dfrac{15(0) + 2(-5\sqrt{3}) + 3(5\sqrt{3})}{15 + 2 + 3} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{20} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$

The y-coordinate of the center of mass is:
$y_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1 y_1 + m_2 y_2 + m_3 y_3}{m_1 + m_2 + m_3} = \dfrac{15(2.5) + 2(-2.5) + 3(-2.5)}{20} = \dfrac{37.5 - 12.5}{20} = \dfrac{25}{20} = 1.25$

The position of the center of mass is $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}, 1.25\right)$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}, 1.25\right)$

questions.q: Two blocks of masses $2$ kg and $1$ kg respectively, are tied to the ends of a string which passes over a light frictionless pulley as shown in the figure below. The masses are held at rest at the same horizontal level and then released. The distance traversed by the centre of mass in $2$ s is _______ m. (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
The acceleration of the blocks in the Atwood machine is given by:

$a = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2} g$

Substituting the given values ($m_1 = 2$ kg, $m_2 = 1$ kg):

$a = \dfrac{2 - 1}{2 + 1} g = \dfrac{g}{3}$

Taking the downward direction as positive, the acceleration of the $2$ kg block is $a_1 = \dfrac{g}{3}$ and the acceleration of the $1$ kg block is $a_2 = -\dfrac{g}{3}$.

The acceleration of the centre of mass is:

$a_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1 a_1 + m_2 a_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

$a_{cm} = \dfrac{2 \left(\dfrac{g}{3}\right) + 1 \left(-\dfrac{g}{3}\right)}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{g}{3}}{3} = \dfrac{g}{9}$

Since the system is released from rest, the initial velocity of the centre of mass is zero.

The distance traversed by the centre of mass in $t = 2$ s is:

$S_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{2} a_{cm} t^2$

$S_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{10}{9}\right) (2)^2 = \dfrac{20}{9} \approx 2.22 \text{ m}$

Answer: $2.22$

questions.q:
The position of an object having mass $0.1$ kg as a function of time $t$ is given as $\vec{r} = \left(10t^2\hat{i} + 5t^3\hat{j}\right)$ m. At $t = 1$ s, which of the following statements are correct?
A. The linear momentum $\vec{p} = \left(2\hat{i} + 1.5\hat{j}\right)$ kg·m/s.
B. The force acting on the object $\vec{F} = \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\right)$ N.
C. The angular momentum of the object about its origin $\vec{L} = 15\hat{k}$ J·s.
D. The torque acting on the object about its origin $\vec{\tau} = 20\hat{k}$ N·m.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Given the position vector $\vec{r} = 10t^2\hat{i} + 5t^3\hat{j}$

Velocity $\vec{v} = \dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = 20t\hat{i} + 15t^2\hat{j}$

Acceleration $\vec{a} = \dfrac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = 20\hat{i} + 30t\hat{j}$

At $t = 1$ s:
$\vec{r} = 10\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}$ m
$\vec{v} = 20\hat{i} + 15\hat{j}$ m/s
$\vec{a} = 20\hat{i} + 30\hat{j}$ m/s$^2$

Linear momentum $\vec{p} = m\vec{v} = 0.1(20\hat{i} + 15\hat{j}) = 2\hat{i} + 1.5\hat{j}$ kg$\cdot$m/s (Statement A is correct)

Force $\vec{F} = m\vec{a} = 0.1(20\hat{i} + 30\hat{j}) = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ N (Statement B is correct)

Angular momentum $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = (10\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}) \times (2\hat{i} + 1.5\hat{j}) = (10 \times 1.5 - 5 \times 2)\hat{k} = 5\hat{k}$ J$\cdot$s (Statement C is incorrect)

Torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = (10\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}) \times (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) = (10 \times 3 - 5 \times 2)\hat{k} = 20\hat{k}$ N$\cdot$m (Statement D is correct)

Therefore, statements A, B, and D are correct.

Answer: A, B and D only

questions.q: A body of mass 14 kg initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio $2: 2: 3$. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of $18 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is $\_\_\_\_$\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution:
From mass ratio 2:2:3 with total mass 14 kg: individual masses are 4 kg, 4 kg, and 6 kg.
Setting coordinate axes along the motion directions of the two equal fragments: fragment 1 has momentum $\vec{p_1} = 4 \times 18\hat{i} = 72\hat{i}$ kg⋅m/s, and fragment 2 has $\vec{p_2} = 4 \times 18\hat{j} = 72\hat{j}$ kg⋅m/s.
By momentum conservation, initially at rest: $\vec{p_1} + \vec{p_2} + \vec{p_3} = 0$, so $\vec{p_3} = -72\hat{i} - 72\hat{j}$ kg⋅m/s.
Velocity of 6 kg fragment: $\vec{v_3} = \frac{\vec{p_3}}{6} = -12\hat{i} - 12\hat{j}$ m/s.
Speed: $|\vec{v_3}| = \sqrt{144 + 144} = \sqrt{288} = 12\sqrt{2}$ m/s.

questions.q: In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses 15 kg and 25 kg, moving in opposite directions with speeds of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in ${ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is : (specific heat of sphere material $31 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{kg}.{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $1 \mathrm{cal}=4.2 \mathrm{~J}$)
questions.solution:
Using conservation of momentum:
$m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = (m_1 + m_2)v_f$ where $v_2 = -30$ m/s (opposite direction).
$15(10) + 25(-30) = 40v_f \Rightarrow v_f = -15$ m/s
Initial kinetic energy:
$KE_i = \frac{1}{2}(15)(10)^2 + \frac{1}{2}(25)(30)^2 = 750 + 11250 = 12000$ J
Final kinetic energy:
$KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(40)(15)^2 = 4500$ J
Heat produced:
$Q = 12000 - 4500 = 7500$ J $= \frac{7500}{4.2} = 1785.71$ cal
Temperature rise:
$\Delta T = \frac{Q}{m_{total} \cdot c} = \frac{1785.71}{40 \times 31} = 1.44°C$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles.
Statement II: The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t to the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution:
Statement I: Total kinetic energy of a system equals $\sum_i \frac{1}{2}m_i v_i^2$. This is TRUE by definition.
Statement II: Total KE can be decomposed as $KE_{total} = \frac{1}{2}M v_{cm}^2 + \sum_i \frac{1}{2}m_i v_i'^2$, where the first term is kinetic energy of center of mass motion and the second is kinetic energy of particles relative to the center of mass. This is TRUE by the energy decomposition theorem (Koenig's theorem).
Both statements are true.

questions.q: A uniform rod $AB$ of mass $2kg$ and Length $30cm$ at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. An impulse of force $0 . 2Ns$ is applied to end B. The time taken by the rod to turn through at right angles will be $\dfrac{\pi}{x}s,$ where $x =$ ____.
questions.solution:
Impulse $J = 0 . 2Ns$

$⇒ J = ∫ Fdt = 0 . 2Ns$

Now, angular impulse $( \overset{\to}{M} )$ will be

${M}_{c} = ∫ τdt$

$= ∫ F\dfrac{L}{2}dt$

$= \dfrac{L}{2} ∫ Fdt = \dfrac{L}{2} \times J$

$= \dfrac{0 . 3}{2} \times 0 . 2$

$= 0 . 03$

Moment of inertia of the rod about the centre of mass, ${I}_{cm} = \dfrac{M{L}^{2}}{12} = \dfrac{2 \times ( 0 . 3{)}^{2}}{12} = \dfrac{0 . 09}{6}$

Angular impulse will be equal to the change in angular momentum.

$M = {I}_{cm}\left({\omega}_{f} - {\omega}_{i}\right)$

$⇒ 0 . 03 = \dfrac{0 . 09}{6}\left({\omega}_{f}\right)$

$⇒ {\omega}_{f} = 2rad{s}^{- 1}$

For angular displacement, we can write $\theta = \omegat$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{\theta}{\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{2 \times 2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}s$.

Therefore, $x = 4$.

questions.q: The identical spheres each of mass $2M$ are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to $4m$ each. Taking point of intersection of these two sides as origin, the magnitude of position vector of the centre of mass of the system is $\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{x}$, where the value of $x$ is ________.
questions.solution:
Position vector $\overset{\to}{r}COM = \dfrac{{m}_{1}\overset{\to}{r}1 + {m}_{2}\overset{\to}{r}2 + {m}_{3}\overset{\to}{r}3}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2} + {m}_{3}}$

$\overset{\to}{r}\text{COM} = \dfrac{2M \times 0 + 2M \times 4\overset{^}{i} + 2M \times 4\overset{^}{j}}{6M}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{r} = \dfrac{4}{3}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{4}{3}\overset{^}{j}$

$| \overset{\to}{r} | = \sqrt{{\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$

Therefore, $x = 3$.

questions.q: A body of mass $1000kg$ is moving horizontally with a velocity $6m{s}^{- 1}$. If $200kg$ extra mass is added, the final velocity (in $m{s}^{- 1}$) is:
questions.solution:
From the conservation of linear momentum, it can be written that

$Mu = \left(M + m\right)v . . . \left(1\right)$

where, $M$ is the initial mass, $u$ is the initial velocity, $m$ is the extra mass added and $v$ is the final velocity of the composition.

From equation (1), it follows that

$1000 \times 6 = 1200 \times v ⇒ v = 5m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two bodies are having kinetic energies in the ratio $16: 9 .$ If they have same linear momentum, the ratio of their masses respectively is:
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy and the momentum of a moving object are related by

$K = \dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m} . . . \left(1\right)$

Hence, the ratio of the kinetic energies of two objects having masses $m$ and $m '$ can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{K}{{K}^{'}} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m}}{\dfrac{{p}^{2}}{2m '}} \\ & = & \dfrac{m '}{m} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the ratio of the kinetic energies into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the ratio of their masses.

$\begin{cases} & ⇒ & \dfrac{16}{9} = \dfrac{m '}{m} \\ & ⇒ & m: m ' = 9: 16\end{cases}$

After collision,

time for collision ${t}_{1} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2gh}}$

so time ,

questions.q: A body of mass $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ falls freely from a height of $100 \mathrm{~m}$, on a platform of mass $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ which is mounted on a spring having spring constant $\mathrm{k}=1.25 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$. The bodysticks to the platform and the spring's maximum compression is found to be $x$. Given that $g=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2},$ the value of $\mathrm{x}$ will be close to :
questions.solution: Velocity of $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ block just before it collides with $3 \mathrm{~kg}$ block $=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}}=\sqrt{2000} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Using principle of conservation of linear momentum just before and just after collision, we get $1 \times \sqrt{2000}=4 \mathrm{v} \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}=\frac{\sqrt{2000}}{4} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Initial compression of spring $1.25 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{x}_{0}=30 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}_{0} \approx 0$ using work energy theorem, $\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{g}}+\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{sp}}=\Delta \mathrm{KE}$\Rightarrow 40 \times x+\frac{1}{2} \times 1.25 \times 10^{6}\left(0^{2}-x^{2}\right)$=0-\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times v^{2}$ solving $x \approx 4 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: Three blocks $A, B$ and $C$ are lying on a smooth horizontal surface, as shown in the figure. $A$ and $B$ have equal masses, $m$ while $C$ has mass $M .$ Block $A$ is given an initial speed $v$ towards $B$ due to which it collides with $B$ perfectly inelastically. The combined mass collides with $C,$ also perfectly inelastically . $\dfrac{5}{6}\text{t}\text{h}$ of the initial kinetic energy is lost in the whole process. What is the value of $M / m$?
questions.solution:
$mv = \left(m + m\right){v}^{′}$

$\left(m + m\right){v}^{′} = \left(m + m + M\right){v}_{f}$

$∴$ final velocity ${v}_{f} = \dfrac{m}{2m + M}v$

Initial energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}$

Final energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m + M\right){\left(\dfrac{mv}{2m + M}\right)}^{2}$

Given that $\dfrac{5}{6}\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m + M\right){\left(\dfrac{mv}{2m + M}\right)}^{2}$

$\dfrac{1}{12}m{v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{m}^{2}{v}^{2}}{\left(2m + M\right)}$

$6m = 2m + M$

$\dfrac{M}{m} = 4$

questions.q: A uniform thin rod AB of length $L$ has linear mass density $\mu\left(x\right) = a + \dfrac{bx}{L}$, where $x$ is measured from A. If the CM of the rod lies at a distance of $\left(\dfrac{7}{12}L\right)$ from A, then $a and b$ are related as:
questions.solution:
Consider an infinitesimal small element of length $dx$ and mars density $\lambda$

${x}_{cm} = \dfrac{∫ \left(dm\right)x}{∫ dm} = \dfrac{∫ \left(\lambdadx\right)x}{∫ \lambdadx}$

$= \dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{L}\left(a + \dfrac{b}{L}x\right)xdx}{{∫}_{0}^{L}\left(a + \dfrac{b}{L}x\right)dx}$

$= \dfrac{{∫}_{0}^{L}axdx + {∫}_{0}^{L}\dfrac{b}{L}{x}^{2}dx}{{∫}_{0}^{L}adx + {∫}_{0}^{L}\dfrac{b}{L}xdx}$

$= \dfrac{a{\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{L} + \dfrac{b}{L}{\left[\dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3}\right]}_{0}^{L}}{a{\left[x\right]}_{0}^{L} + \dfrac{b}{L}{\left[\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{0}^{L}}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{a}{2}\left({L}^{2} - {0}^{2}\right) + \dfrac{b}{3L}\left({L}^{3} - {0}^{3}\right)}{a\left(L - 0\right) + \dfrac{b}{2L}\left({L}^{2} - {0}^{2}\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{a}{2}{L}^{2} + \dfrac{b{L}^{2}}{3}}{aL + \dfrac{bL}{2}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{a}{2}L + \dfrac{bL}{3}}{a + \dfrac{b}{2}}$

$∵ {x}_{cm} = \dfrac{7L}{12} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{a}{2} + \dfrac{b}{3}\right)L}{a + \dfrac{b}{2}} ⇒ \dfrac{7}{12} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3a + 2b}{6}}{\dfrac{2a + b}{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{7}{12} = \dfrac{3a + 2b}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{\left(2a + b\right)} ⇒ 7\left(2a + b\right) = 4\left(3a + 2b\right)$

$⇒ 14a + 7b = 12a + 8b ⇒ 2a = b$

questions.solution:
Let the mass of solid cylinder is $M$ and angle with vertical is $\theta$. Now, we take a small element of thickness $d y$ at a distance $y$ from the vertex. The radius of small element is $r$, as shown in the figure below.

Then, $tan \theta = \dfrac{R}{h} = \dfrac{r}{y}$ which will give, $r = ytan \theta$. The density of the cone is given by,

$ρ = \dfrac{M}{\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\pi{R}^{2}h} = \dfrac{3M}{\pi{R}^{2}h}$.

The mass of the small element is given by,

$d M = ρ d V$

$d M = \dfrac{3M}{\pi{R}^{2}h} \times \pi{r}^{2} d y = \dfrac{3M{y}^{2}\tan^{2}\theta}{{R}^{2}h} d y$

The center of mass of the cone is given by,

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{M}{∫}_{0}^{h}y d M$

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{M}{∫}_{0}^{h}y \cdot \dfrac{3M{y}^{2}\tan^{2}\theta}{{R}^{2}h} d y$

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{3}{{R}^{2}h}{\left(\dfrac{R}{h}\right)}^{2}{\left[\dfrac{{y}^{4}}{4}\right]}_{0}^{h}$

${z}_{0} = \dfrac{3h}{4}$.

This question has $Statement - I$ and $Statement - II$ of the four choices given after the Statements, choose the one that best describes the two Statements.

$Statement - I:$ A point particle of mass $m$ moving with speed $ν$ collides with stationary point particle of mass $M$. If the maximum energy loss possible is given as
$f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}m{ν}^{2}\right)$ then $f = \left(\dfrac{m}{M + m}\right)$.

$Statement - II:$ Maximum energy loss occurs when the particles get stuck together as a result of the collision.
options: Statement-$I$ is true, Statement-$II$ is false.
Statement-$I$ is false, Statement-$II$ is true.
Statement-$I$ is true, Statement-$II$ is true, Statement-$II$ is a correct explanation of Statement-$I$.
Statement-$I$ is true, Statement-$II$ is true, Statement-$II$ is not a correct explanation of Statement-$I$.
questions.solution:
Maximum energy loss will take place in perfectly inelastic collision, and is given by, $∆ K = \dfrac{{P}^{2}}{2m} - \dfrac{{P}^{2}}{2\left(m + M\right)}$
$⇒ ∆ K = \dfrac{{P}^{2}}{2m}\left[1 - \dfrac{m}{\left(m + M\right)}\right]$
$⇒ ∆ K = \dfrac{{P}^{2}}{2m}\left[\dfrac{M}{\left(m + M\right)}\right]$
$⇒ ∆ K = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}\left[\dfrac{M}{\left(m + M\right)}\right]$
On comparing with the given form of equation, we have, $\left(f = \dfrac{M}{m + M}\right)$

Hence Statement-$I$ is false, Statement-$II$ is true. ( As it is perfect Inelastic collision)
